summary: I measured the real FontConverter and TypingEngine (built from the snapshot in r3\guj-audit\repo) against Shree's own composers byte for byte. The composer answers are fresh S8GujU64/S8Guj764 captures from this run: all 19 vendor .GUJ keyboards, a sweep of 206 codes and 69 code runs, each read twice and stable. SLNXT's shared memory was dumped before the captures and written back afterwards; a final dump of all 10 SL8_* mappings matches the first one. The last round's result holds: syllables and whole typed words come out right. 5,536 words typed key by key give exactly FontConverter's bytes in both families at every keystroke, and 323 of 330 distinct words equal Shree's own spellings joined together. The other 7 are explained in the notes. The client's 'many bugs' are elsewhere, and I found 15 (3 HIGH): (1) Backspace after a key that finished one of the chart's multi-key sequences deletes every key of that sequence. ક then ે then Backspace leaves nothing. This hits 16% of Backspace positions. (2) રુ and રૂ are written as ર plus a sign hanging below it, where the fonts have the ligatures that Shree's own ru/ruu keys type. (3) Converting a .docx puts the Shree font on English runs too, so English words turn into Gujarati glyphs. The rest are MEDIUM/LOW: the Eng keyboard types Latin letters, 17 ASCII punctuation marks show as Gujarati glyphs without any warning, ॥ and ₹ are not mapped (they become '?' in .txt), 78 chart 'A or B' entries were stored as one key sequence, Ekl types nothing, code EE (a dash) is missing, plus reading-back and edge issues. Nothing was fixed, the main checkout was not touched, and no UI, Word or keyboard hook was used.
counts:
L1 per key: 19 vendor keyboards x (94 printed keys + 38 Ctrl+Space keys) = 2,508 positions. Shree types something on 2,117. Unicode, 7 bytes and 4/5/6 bytes are all identical on 1,911.
- (a) TextSoft types nothing where Shree types: 1 (InScript z; Shree types a space).
- (b) Same Unicode, different 7 bytes: 134 (89 for 4/5/6). By cause: ru/ruu ligature keys 30, half-letter keys pressed alone 33, code EE 15, reph key alone 14, candra B5 vs B8 23 and anusvara+reph 84 AE vs AF 1 (both are spellings the composer itself accepts), nukta '9C 00' 18 (a composer artefact).
- (c) Different Unicode: 46. ENG 19 (Latin letters, ASCII digits and punctuation); PHONETIC 27 (consonant key alone: chart gives the half form, composer the full letter).
- (d) Vowel-key-alone quirks: 25.
- Shree types nothing but TextSoft types something: 349 (298 Ctrl+Space fallbacks, 29 Shift fallbacks, 22 codes neither composer answers).
- Ctrl+Shift+1 layer: 14 chart symbols x 21 layouts = 294; 210 identical, 84 differ (the ₹ $, ॥ |, [ [ and ] ] keys on every layout).
- Chart-only keyboards: Ekl has 70 of 106 key sequences that can never start, and 0 of 330 words can be typed. 78 sequences in 18 layouts contain a literal 'or'.

L2 typing: 330 real words and 17 lines with punctuation, digits and Enter, on the 19 non-phonetic layouts (Eng is type-by-sound and was covered under L1), in Unicode, SHREE-GUJ7 and SHREE-GUJ profiles.
- 5,536 word key-plans were checked on the real engine.
- Final buffer = FontConverter(word) in 5,536 of 5,536 for both families.
- Every intermediate state = FontConverter(the Unicode shown at that point): 0 mismatches.
- Against the composer: 323 of 330 distinct words equal Shree's spellings joined together. The other 7: 6 end in a virama, where TextSoft writes the visible halant and the composer its half form; 1 has no ground-truth piece.
- Backspace: 4,576 of 28,537 positions (16.0%) remove more than the last keystroke, the same in all three profiles.
- A mouse click before the word: 0 problems. All typed lines matched the converter.
- Typing order: TextSoft's result does not depend on order (checked on 387 reph-first words).

L3 symbols: 152 characters (95 printable ASCII + 57 symbols), alone and between letters, both tables = 608 conversions. Fonts were drawn by glyph index (SHREE-GUJ7-0750, SHREE-GUJ-0750, Shree-Guj7-001).
- Confirmed: 17 ASCII characters (" # $ & < > @ [ \ ] ^ _ ` { | } ~) draw another glyph, a blank or no glyph, and none is reported.
- Refuted: ':' (byte 3A draws a colon).
- Confirmed: – — ÷ ૰ are written as U+0081, U+0081 U+0081, U+008D, U+008F, which are the composer's own bytes 81, 81 81, 8D, 8F.
- Refuted: ', . ( ) 1 ? !' are not shown as 'had no mapping' (ConverterViewModel.cs:274 drops anything up to U+007F), although FontConverter does list them.
- 11 characters (₹ ॥ ૱ and 8 others such as U+2212 minus, ZWSP, BOM) pass through as non-font code points; ° and 11 others are dropped (reported).
- All 18 installed GUJ7/GUJ fonts have no glyph at 0x3C, the byte Shree writes for ₹.

L4 reading back: 42,832 reads.
- Shree truth, 17,335 strings per family: 17,061 (98.4%) read exactly. All 274 differences are lossy font spellings (228 vowel signs ૢ ૣ the fonts cannot show, 42 virama, 4 ઇઁ read as ઇં).
- 6,000 joined composer words: 5,782 exact. Per-key composer bytes: 158/160. Code sweep: 97/116. Code runs: 32/40. TextSoft's own L3 output: 43/152 read back unchanged. L2 words and lines: 690/694 round trip.
- Fuzz of 91,125 three-character strings per family: 2 U+FDD3 leaks; 1,373 strings change on the round trip, 18 of them realistic.
- The 4 named open items are confirmed: in-word ZWNJ halant dropped, 22 22 / 27 27 read as ‘‘ ’’, … comes back as '...', U+FDD3 leak. 'B7 reads as •' is correct (B7 draws a bullet).

L5 fonts: 'Shree-Lipi 7.0' lists 9 faces, all installed, all on the shree-guj7 table. '4.0/5.0/6.0' lists 7 SHREE-GUJ-* faces, installed, on shree-guj456. WPF sees 19 Shree GUJ families (plus Akruti, Hitarth and ITRFK). No cross-family font in the typing lists. The Converter's font box adds every installed font. An old saved '7.0 + SHREE-GUJ-0750' setting reopens silently on SHREE-GUJ7-0750.

L6 outputs: 196 code points (everything the tables can write, plus ASCII, markers and pass-through characters).
- .txt (Windows-1252) changes 16: 12 become '?' (₹ ॥ ૱ and the U+FDDx markers among them), 3 become '-', 1 becomes "'".
- .rtf (WPF) and .docx keep all 196.
- The C1 bytes 81 8D 8F 90 survive every file path.
- Mixed .docx: the English run is restamped SHREE-GUJ7-0750.

bugs.title: Backspace after a key that completed a chart run deletes every key of the run (the consonant vanishes)
bugs.repro: Any layout, any profile (Unicode, SHREE-GUJ7-0750, SHREE-GUJ-0750). InScript: press k then s (chart run 'ks' = કે), then Backspace. Also: InScript m d (સ્) + BS; InScript k e (કા) + BS; BPMK s f (કા) + BS; Phonetic g a (ગ) + BS; Typewriter H k + BS. Harness: harness.exe type gu-inscript "ks<BS>" "md<BS>"
bugs.textsoft: SHREE-GUJ7: after k s the app holds 4C A1 24; Backspace sends 3 backspaces → buffer empty (ક lost). m d (6B B9) + BS → empty. Unicode: 0A95 0AC7 + BS → empty. Retyping the rest then gives e.g. A1 64 (sign with no letter).
bugs.shree: The composer works code by code, so Backspace removes the last keystroke and ક (4C 24) stays; after m d, સ (6B) stays. TextSoft's own docs/KEYBOARDS.md promises 'Backspace takes back the last key struck'.
bugs.cause: src/FontSoftware.Engine/TypingEngine.cs Emit(): when a run grows (replace>0), DropPieces(replace) drops the earlier keys' pieces and AddPiece records the whole run text as ONE piece (typing-order path lines 539-543, legacy path 552-558, Unicode path 567-568). HandleBackspace (lines 882-905 and 926-933) then PopPiece()s that one piece and deletes every key of the run.
bugs.fix: Keep one piece per keystroke inside a run. Either push only the growth (AddPiece(output.Length - replace) when the new run text starts with the old one), or keep a stack of run states (key prefix → text) so Backspace restores the previous state (_seqKeys.Length--, _seqOut = text of the prefix) and re-renders it. Add tests: InScript 'ks'+BS = ક (4C 24), 'md'+BS = સ (6B), Phonetic 'ga'+BS = ગ્.
bugs.evidence: 4,576 of 28,537 Backspace positions (16.0%) in 5,536 typed words on 19 layouts, identical in all 3 profiles. Per layout: Phonet86 11.8%, InScript 12.3%, Akshar 12.3%, BPMK 12.8%, ITR 13.5%, Typewriter 19.6%, Newroma 21.1%, Phonetic 50.0% (results/l2-backspace-per-layout.json).

bugs.title: રુ and રૂ are written as ર plus a hanging sign (66 79 / 66 7C); the ligatures Shree's ru/ruu keys type are never written, and the new-ruu glyph 7E is not read back
bugs.repro: Typing with SHREE-GUJ7-0750 or SHREE-GUJ-0750: ITR Shift+H, InScript Shift+J, Typewriter # and :, DOE Ctrl+Space b/n/o, BPMK/Remington Ctrl+Space v, Akshar Ctrl+Space x, Asterix Ctrl+Space j, Crtronic :, Script ?, Roma _, MTNK Ctrl+Space l, Newroma Ctrl+Space b/l (30 keys in total). Converter Unicode→Shree-Lipi 7 on 'ગુરુ રૂપિયા'.
bugs.textsoft: ITR Shift+H → 66 7C. Typewriter # → 66 79. Typewriter : → 66 7C (VS1 dropped). Converter: 4E 79 66 79 20 66 7C 72 60 65 70, drawn as ર with the u/uu hook hanging under it (results/png/strips-1.png). Reverse table: 7E 24 reads '~', unmapped.
bugs.shree: S8Guj764 writes code 7E → EA 24 (old રૂ ligature), EA → 7E 24 (new રૂ), E9 → 7B 24 (રુ). With anusvara: 7B 84 24 / EA 84 24 / 7E 84 24. With reph: 7B AE 24. With visarga: 7B 24 3A. Each draws the proper joined shape (results/composer-sequences.json runs2, results/png/strips-reph.png).
bugs.cause: assets/config/mappings/unicode-to-shree-guj7.json and unicode-to-shree-guj456.json have no pairs for રુ, રૂ or રૂ︀; only ર→66, ુ→79, ૂ→7C. unicode-to-shree-gujx.json does have them (રુ→U+E3C5, રૂ→U+E3CA, રૂ︀→U+E3C6). shree-guj7-to-unicode.json reads 7B→રુ and EA→રૂ but has no pair for 7E. The last round's truth spelled રુ/રૂ from ર and the sign fed as two separate codes.
bugs.fix: In both families add 'રુ'→'{$' (7B 24), 'રૂ'→'ê$' (EA 24, the old shape, as gujx does) and 'રૂ︀'→'~$' (7E 24). The existing post rules then move ં, reph and ઃ to where the composer puts them. In both reverse tables add '~$' and '~' → 'રૂ︀'. Update ShreeComposerTruthTests/Data to accept the ligature spellings.
bugs.evidence: L1: 30 vendor keys where Shree writes a ligature and TextSoft writes ra + sign. 10 of the 330 common test words contain રુ or રૂ (ગુરુ, ગુરુવાર, રૂપ, રૂપિયા, શરૂ, ભરૂચ, ઝરૂખો, રુચિ…).

bugs.title: Converting .docx/.rtf puts the Shree font on English runs too: English words, e-mails and ASCII symbols turn into Gujarati glyphs
bugs.repro: Converter Files mode, Unicode → Shree-Lipi 7.0 (SHREE-GUJ7-0750), on a .docx with the runs 'ગુજરાત સરકાર ' (Nirmala UI) and bold 'Email: info@gujarat.gov.in [1] & "Notice" #5 ' (results/files/mixed-unicode.docx, run through FileConversion.ConvertFile by harness.exe docx).
bugs.textsoft: Both runs come out with font SHREE-GUJ7-0750. The English run keeps its bytes 45 6D 61 69 6C 3A 20 69 6E 66 6F 40 … 23 35 20, which the font draws as ઊળફશલઃ … ઽ … × ૫ (results/files/mixed-to-guj7.docx). The Converter's text mode does the same: Latin passes through and is shown in the legacy font.
bugs.shree: Shree has no codes for Latin letters (code sweep: 0 of 206 codes type A–Z or a–z), so Shree never writes English into a Shree font. TextSoft's own policy (tools/Shared/ShreeNonIndic.cs) is 'English text is set in an English font'.
bugs.cause: src/FontSoftware.App/Services/FileConversion.cs ConvertParts lines 223-247 restamps RunFonts on every run group whatever its text. RichTextConversion.Convert lines 31-38 sets FontFamily on every run.
bugs.fix: Convert and restamp only runs that contain Indic text, or text in the source legacy font; leave runs that are only Latin/ASCII with their own font. Split a mixed run at its Latin stretches. In text mode, report Latin letters that would land in a Shree font.

bugs.title: Eng (type-by-sound) keyboard types raw Latin letters or ASCII where Shree's ENG.GUJ types Gujarati
bugs.repro: Eng layout, SHREE-GUJ7-0750: type 'laxmi', 'zaveri', 'Ishvar'. Single keys: x z I G Y J F ~ & < @ # $ > _ (Shree maps them); also B C K P Q V W X Z q [ \ ] ^ ` { | } (Shree types nothing).
bugs.textsoft: 'laxmi' → 67 78 72 64 (x = 0x78 glyph). 'zaveri' → 7A 41 68 A1 71 66. I → 49, G → 47, Y → 59, J → 4A, F → 46, ~ → 7E (new-ruu glyph), & → 26 (bar only), < → 3C (no glyph), @ → 40 (ઽ), # → 23 (×), $ → 24 (blank), > → 3E, _ → 5F (ન). Unicode profile shows the Latin letters.
bugs.cause: assets/config/translit/gujarati-shree-eng.json has no entries for x z I G Y J F. TypingEngine.HandlePhonetic buffers only A–Z (TryRomanChar, TypingEngine.cs:1029-1041), so the scheme's own specials '&'→।, '-'→ઽ, '~'→ૃ can never be reached, and every non-letter passes raw (lines 994-1000). Letters the scheme cannot read are rendered as Latin.
bugs.fix: Add x→ક્ષ, z→ઝ, I→ઇ, G→૰, Y→્ય, J→઼, F→ૢ to the scheme, as ENG.GUJ maps them. Send & ~ < @ # $ > _ through the layout or scheme instead of passing them raw. Swallow Latin letters the scheme cannot read (Shree types nothing for them).
bugs.evidence: 30 Eng keys differ in 7 bytes (results/l1-compare.json keyboards.ENG, composer-vendor-keys.json ENG).

bugs.title: 17 ASCII characters are written as codes the Shree fonts draw as Gujarati glyphs, blanks or nothing, and none is reported
bugs.repro: Converter Unicode→Shree-Lipi 7 or 4/5/6, or the typist toggles to English, or a layout passes the key raw. E.g. 'ક[ક]ક', 'A & B', '"હા"', '#5', 'a@b'. Ctrl+Shift+1 [ and ] (chart symbols on all 21 layouts).
bugs.textsoft: Pass-through bytes and what the fonts draw there: " → 22 ‘ (also for closing quotes); # → 23 ×; $ → 24 blank spacer; & → 26 danda bar; < → 3C (no glyph in any of the 18 installed fonts); > → 3E blank; @ → 40 ઽ; [ → 5B long i-sign; \ → 5C થ; ] → 5D ીં; ^ → 5E ધ; _ → 5F ન; ` → 60 પ; { → 7B રુ; | → 7C ૂ; } → 7D ીર્; ~ → 7E new રૂ. Example 'ક[ક]ક' → 4C 24 5B 4C 24 5D 4C 24, drawn as ક િક ીં. Converter status says nothing. ':' is fine (3A draws a colon).
bugs.shree: No Shree code types any of these characters. Codes 5B '[' and 5D ']' (U composer) → S8Guj764 writes nothing, and the run '[ક' → 4C 24. So Shree never puts these bytes in for the ASCII characters.
bugs.cause: unicode-to-shree-guj7.json / guj456.json have no ASCII pairs (NonIndic.Complete only covers U+00A0 and up, tools/Shared/ShreeNonIndic.cs FontCodes). FontConverter passes unmatched characters through (FontConverter.cs:96-105). ConverterViewModel.cs:273-274 drops everything ≤U+007F from the report. Layout symbols '[=[' and ']=]' in every assets/config/layouts/guj-*.json (e.g. guj-itr.json line 763).
bugs.fix: Add pairs to both tables for the 17 characters: '"' → 22 22 (or 27 27 when it closes), the rest → "" with unmapped:true (left out and reported), never the script byte. Report characters that the target font draws as script even when ≤U+007F. Drop or remap Ctrl+Shift+1 [ and ] for the 7 and 4/5/6 families.
bugs.evidence: results/l3-symbols.json, results/png/strips-1.png (last row), l1-compare.json symbolLayer (42 key positions).

bugs.title: ॥, ₹ and ૱ are left as Unicode in legacy output ('?' in .txt), ° is dropped, and 3C reads back as '<'
bugs.repro: Type Ctrl+Shift+1 | (॥) or Ctrl+Shift+1 $ (₹) with a Shree-Lipi 7 or 4/5/6 font. Or convert 'સત્યમેવ જયતે॥ કિંમત ₹૫૦૦ ૩૦°' to Shree-Lipi 7, as .txt and as .docx.
bugs.textsoft: ॥ → U+0965 and ₹ → U+20B9 inserted as Unicode, which the fonts do not draw (fallback font or box). .txt: 71 4C 84 24 64 73 20 3F 35 30 30 … A1 3F (both become '?'). ° is dropped. Reverse: 3C → '<' (unmapped); 97 26 26 → '।।'.
bugs.shree: ॥ typed as two dandas (codes D3 D3) → 97 26 26, which draws a double bar. The direct ॥ code F9 → nothing. ₹ (code F8) → 3C, but none of the 18 installed GUJ7/GUJ fonts has a glyph at 0x3C. ૱ (EB) → nothing.
bugs.cause: No pair for U+0965 or U+20B9 in unicode-to-shree-guj7/guj456.json, so they pass through (FontConverter.cs:96-105). FileConversion.WriteTxt (FileConversion.cs:96-100) encodes with Windows-1252, which turns them into 3F. No reverse pair for 3C or 97 26 26.
bugs.fix: Forward ॥ → 97 26 26 (Shree's spelling); reverse 97 26 26 → ॥ (longest match before 97 26). ₹: reverse 3C → ₹. Forward: either write 3C (byte parity, but invisible in today's fonts) or keep U+20B9 for typing/docx and write a visible substitute in .txt, with a warning. ° → 8F (the font's circle). Never let WriteTxt turn a character into '?' silently.
bugs.evidence: results/l6-output-paths.json, results/l6-files.json, l1-compare.json symbolLayer (42 key positions), composer-sequences.json (73 F9 → 4C 24; D3 D3 → 97 26 26).

bugs.title: The charts' 'A or B' entries were stored as one key sequence 'AorB': 78 dead sequences in 18 layouts, whose prefixes change what nearby keys type
bugs.repro: ITR: type ; T ; (ત્ત) then o (reph key), then space. InScript: $ k o. Ekl: k o r > a. Harness: harness.exe type guj-itr ";T;o "
bugs.textsoft: ITR ';T;o ' → D1 66 B9 20 (ત્ત followed by a visible ર્) instead of D1 AE 20. Only a following sign repairs it (';T;ot' → D1 AE 70). Backspace also removes the whole pseudo-run. Ekl 'kor>a' → 66 4C B9 24, not ક.
bugs.shree: The reph struck after its letter always lands on that letter: ત્ત + reph → D1 AE (typewriter order, as in 'fo' = 4C AE 24).
bugs.cause: Key sequences that contain a literal 'or', taken from the chart's 'A or B' cells. Ekl 28 (guj-ekl.json line 345 'kor>a'=ક), Eng 7, Asterix 5, Phonetic 4, Remington 1 4, BPMK 3, Crtronic 3, Indica 3, Modular 3, Roma 3, Script 3, InScript 2 ('$korjdk'=ર્ક), ITR 2 (guj-itr.json line 607 ';T;orØo'=ત્ત), Phonet86 2, Remington 2 2, Typewriter 2, DOE 1, Newroma 1. Their prefixes make the engine treat the next keys as one run, whose text bypasses TypingOrder.Mark.
bugs.fix: Split every 'AorB' sequence into two sequences A and B, regenerate the layouts with the ChmMap/KbdFromChm fix, and add a ConfigCheck rule that rejects sequences containing 'or' (results/l1-dead-runs.json lists all 78).

bugs.title: The Ekl keyboard types nothing for almost every consonant: the engine drops a key sequence whose first key types nothing on its own
bugs.repro: Layout guj-ekl, any profile: type k a, j a, f a, b a (the chart's runs ka=કા, ja=…, ba=બ).
bugs.textsoft: Every key types nothing and the buffer stays empty. 0 of 330 common words can be typed. 70 of the 106 Ekl sequences can never be started.
bugs.shree: Ekl has a chart but no runtime .GUJ file at Shree. The chart's sequences (ba=બ, ga=ગ, ka=કા, …) are what a typist expects.
bugs.cause: TypingEngine.OnKey lines 480-498: when the first key of a sequence has no single-key output, output is '' and replace is 0, so ResetSequence() runs and the key is swallowed (A-Z, line 493). ResolveSequence (613-623) therefore never sees the second key of the sequence. Ekl's consonant keys have no single-key mapping (guj-ekl.json has 12 keys).
bugs.fix: In OnKey, do not reset when the key only starts or extends a sequence: keep _seqKeys when _layout.SequenceCanGrow(grown) and show nothing yet. Or give Ekl's sequence-starting keys their chart letter as a single-key output.

bugs.title: Code EE (byte 90, a short dash) is missing: TextSoft types the plain key's letter instead, and 90 is not read back
bugs.repro: Ctrl+Space 3 on Akshar, Asterix, BPMK, Crtronic, DOE, ITR, MTNK, Remington, Remington 1, Remington 2, Roma, Script; Ctrl+Space p on Typewriter; > on Eng (15 keys). Profile SHREE-GUJ7-0750.
bugs.textsoft: ITR, Akshar, Asterix, DOE, MTNK and Roma → 33 (૩). BPMK, Remington and Remington 2 → 4F (ઘ). Crtronic and Script → 5E (ધ). Remington 1 → 61 (ફ). Typewriter → 51 (ચ). Reverse: 4C 24 90 4C 24 reads 'ક\u0090ક' (unmapped).
bugs.shree: S8Guj764 writes code EE as 90, which draws a short dash. In runs: 73 EE 73 → 4C 24 90 4C 24; 31 EE 32 → 31 90 32. The U composer has no answer for EE.
bugs.cause: No Unicode character is assigned to EE in assets/config/shree-kbd/GUJ.json or in the layouts, so the Ctrl+Space entries are missing. When a Ctrl+Space key has nothing on its layer, TypingEngine.ResolveSequence (lines 646-649) falls back to the plain key. Neither table has a pair for byte 90.
bugs.fix: Give EE a reading (e.g. U+2010 HYPHEN), add the 15 Ctrl+Space entries to the layouts, add forward U+2010 → 90 and reverse 90 → U+2010 in both families, and add EE to GUJ.json.
bugs.evidence: results/l1-compare.json b7 (15 keys), composer-codes.json EE → 90, composer-sequences.json runs2.

bugs.title: Reading Shree text: a visible halant inside a word is read as a joining virama, and a lone half form is read as a bare virama
bugs.repro: Legacy → Unicode (shree-guj7-to-unicode or guj456) on the composer's own bytes: 4C B9 24 4C 24 (ક્‌ક), 5F B9 5F (ન્‌ન), 4C B9 24 73 (ક્‌ત), 66 B9 4C 24 (ર્‌ક / ર્‍ક), 64 B9 F6 (મ્‌સ્ર્). Also a half form followed by a space, e.g. BC 20.
bugs.textsoft: Reads ક્ક, ન્ન, ક્ત, ર્ક (the visible ra + halant becomes a reph on ક), મ્સ્ર. Writing those back gives BC 4C 24 / 4C AE 24, i.e. different glyphs. BC (ક્‍) reads ક્ and writes back as 4C B9 24.
bugs.shree: The composer writes ક્‌ક = 4C B9 24 4C 24 (visible halant, then ક) and ર્‍ક = 66 B9 4C 24. A half form waiting for its next letter is written ક્‍ = BC.
bugs.cause: shree-guj7-to-unicode.json (and guj456) map B9 '¹' to a plain '્' with no ZWNJ, and the half-form codes to 'C્' with no ZWJ, so a following consonant joins them.
bugs.fix: Reverse pairs: B9 (with its spacer) followed by a consonant → '્‌'; a half-form code not followed by a consonant → 'C્‍'. Add the composer's runs (composer-sequences.json) as read-back tests.
bugs.evidence: results/l4-readback.json named and the 'ZWNJ halant inside a word lost' group; fuzz-forward-leaks.json roundTripSample (18 realistic half-form cases).

bugs.title: Look-alike bytes are read back as their look-alike, not as what was written: 22 22 → ‘‘, 27 27 → ’’, 2E 2E 2E → ..., a colon after a word → visarga
bugs.repro: Legacy → Unicode on TextSoft's own output for “ ” … and on Shree text with a colon, e.g. 'તેણે કહ્યું: "હા".' written to Shree-Lipi 7 and read back.
bugs.textsoft: 22 22 → U+2018 U+2018. 27 27 → U+2019 U+2019. 2E 2E 2E → '...' (FontConverter lists '.' as unmapped). 3A after a letter → ઃ, so 'કહ્યું:' comes back as 'કહ્યુંઃ'. 97 26 26 → '।।'. (B7 → • is right: B7 draws a bullet.)
bugs.shree: Shree types nothing for “ ” (codes F4/F5 give no bytes). Typists write a double quote as two single quotes (22 22). Shree writes both colon (code 3A) and visarga (D4) as 3A.
bugs.cause: shree-guj7-to-unicode.json pairs '"'→‘, "'"→’, ':'→ઃ (line 123). There are no two-byte pairs for 22 22 or 27 27, and no pair for 2E.
bugs.fix: Add reverse pairs 22 22 → “, 27 27 → ”, 2E 2E 2E → …. Read 3A as ':' when it is followed by a space, end or punctuation and the word has no other visarga context (or offer it as an option).
bugs.evidence: results/l4-readback.json named, results/rt-words-back.json (4 changed round trips).

bugs.title: The private marker U+FDD3 leaks into legacy output when ્ન with no letter before it carries an i-sign or a nukta
bugs.repro: Converter Unicode→Shree-Lipi 7 or 4/5/6 on '્નિ' or '્ન઼' (e.g. a halant key pressed at the start of a word, then ન, then the i-sign).
bugs.textsoft: '્નિ' → U+FDD3 72 5F. '્ન઼' → U+FDD3 9C 5F. In .txt the marker becomes 3F '?'.
bugs.shree: The composer writes ્ન alone as ન = 5F, and ન with i-sign / nukta as 72 5F / 9C 5F.
bugs.cause: unicode-to-shree-guj7.json pre-rule at line 15 replaces the virama with U+FDD3, then the i-sign rule (line 30) and nukta rule (line 35) move the sign between U+FDD3 and ન. The pair 'U+FDD3 ન' no longer matches, so U+FDD3 passes through. Same in guj456.
bugs.fix: Include ﷓ in the cluster classes of the i-sign and nukta pre rules, or run the FDD3 rule after them, or add a pair U+FDD3 → "".

bugs.title: Half-letter, link and reph keys pressed alone show the full letter + visible halant (or ra + halant) where Shree shows the half form or reph, and that form stays if the word ends there
bugs.repro: BPMK Shift+A (બ્), Shift+: (સ્), Shift+G (ન્) …, the link key (InScript d), the reph key (ITR o, BPMK ") pressed at the start of a word or before a space. Harness: harness.exe type guj-bpmk "A "
bugs.textsoft: BPMK Shift+A → 62 B9 (બ with halant). With a space after it: 62 B9 20. Reph key alone → 66 B9. Once the next letter comes it is corrected (A i f → E5 65 70).
bugs.shree: Half form while waiting: Shift+A → E5, Shift+: → F5, Shift+G → DE. Reph alone → AE. Followed by a space, E5 20.
bugs.cause: Pre-rule 1 of unicode-to-shree-guj7.json/guj456.json (line 10: a word-final virama becomes the visible halant ્+ZWNJ) is applied to the half-typed word in TypingEngine.RerenderLegacy (lines 811-868). The half-letter keys type 'C્' without ZWJ.
bugs.fix: While a word is being typed, render a trailing virama that came from a half-letter or link key as the half form (append ZWJ for that render). Keep the visible halant only for the explicit halant key, or after a word that has deliberately been ended.
bugs.evidence: 33 half-letter keys + 14 reph keys + 15 link keys (results/l1-compare.json). 6 of 330 words end in a virama (results/l2-composer-pieces.json).

bugs.title: Converter output font box offers every installed font, so a SHREE-GUJ7 face can be stamped on 4/5/6 bytes; an old saved 7.0 setting silently switches font
bugs.repro: Converter: output layout 'Shree-Lipi 4.0/5.0/6.0', output font SHREE-GUJ7-0750 (it is in the list), text 'પઙ્ક્તિ અઙ્ગ'. Main window: start with a setting saved by the committed build, where the 7.0 row's default was shree-guj-0750.
bugs.textsoft: The guj456 table writes ઙ્ક, ઙ્ખ, ઙ્ગ, ઙ્ઘ, ઙ્ક્ષ standing whole as 91, 92, 93, 94, B6. The file is stamped SHREE-GUJ7-0750, where those codes draw પ, થ, ન, સ્ત્ર and a ્રૂ mark. The saved shree-guj-0750 is not in the filtered 7.0 list, so the app silently selects SHREE-GUJ7-0750.
bugs.shree: A 4/5/6 face draws 91-94/B6 as the ઙ conjuncts. The 7 table never writes those codes, so 7 bytes are safe in either family.
bugs.cause: ConverterViewModel.RebuildFonts (around lines 605-625) appends SystemFontService.InstalledFamilies() after the layout's own font, while OutputKey() keeps the layout's encoding. MainViewModel.RestoreDefaultsForLanguage lines 911-920 ignores a saved font that is not in the filtered list, without telling the user.
bugs.fix: For layouts with 'families', list the members (FontLayout.Includes) first and choose the table from the chosen font's family, or refuse a 7↔4/5/6 mismatch. When a saved font is dropped, tell the user which font was chosen instead.
bugs.evidence: results/l5-fontlayouts.json, fonts-installed.json, fonts-wpf-families.json. The typing lists have no cross-family fonts (9 + 7 faces, all correct).

bugs.title: TextSoft types characters where Shree types nothing (and nothing where Shree types a space)
bugs.repro: Ctrl+Space then a key whose third-layer slot is empty in the vendor file (e.g. ITR Ctrl+Space 0, BPMK Ctrl+Space q). Shift on a key whose shifted slot is empty (Newroma Shift+4, MTNK Shift+9, Akshar Shift+\). InScript z.
bugs.textsoft: Ctrl+Space + key types the plain key (ITR Ctrl+Space 0 → 30 ૦; BPMK Ctrl+Space q → 2D). Shift on an empty slot types the normal character (Newroma Shift+4 → 34 ૪). InScript z is swallowed (nothing).
bugs.shree: The composer answers nothing for those 327 key positions (file byte FF). For InScript z the file holds code 20, so Shree types 20 (a space).
bugs.cause: TypingEngine.ResolveSequence lines 646-649 fall back to the single key when nothing on the layer matches. SelectOutput lines 1064-1068 treat a null Shift as 'types the normal character'. OnKey line 493 swallows letter keys with no mapping.
bugs.fix: After an escape, type nothing for a key the layer leaves empty (Shree behaviour). Write "" for empty shifted slots of vendor keyboards (as the importer already does). Map InScript z to a space, or document the difference.

notes:
Composer safety: SLNXT (PID 10232) was running and its SL8_DLL_DATA was all zeros (no keyboard loaded). The Gujarati composer DLLs reset two bytes of SL8_DEFAULTS_DATA (0x90 and 0x92) just by loading; I proved this with a load that captured nothing. After each of the 2 composer sessions I wrote SL8_DLL_DATA and SL8_DEFAULTS_DATA back from the dumps. The final dump of all 10 SL8_* mappings is identical to the one taken before the first load. I wrote the dumps back directly, because no keyboard load can restore an all-zero table. The probe keyboards had to live on a short path (C:\Users\harde\AppData\Local\Temp\r3g); copies are under composer\kbd. One composer process at a time; no UI, Word, clipboard or hook was used. I stopped 3 MSBuild node processes my builds left behind (started 01:44). The main checkout was not touched. I did not run the unit-test suite (an audit does not need it).

What could not be measured here:
- Whether Word draws U+0081/008D/008F/0090 (– — ÷ ૰). They reach Word as \u129? in the RTF paste and as KEYEVENTF_UNICODE characters. They are Shree's own bytes and survive .txt/.rtf/.docx, so this is left for the live Word test.
- Shree's multi-key behaviour on PHONETIC and ENG (the composer only answers single keys; the PHONETIC consonant keys answer the full letter where the chart gives the half form).
- Shree's spelling of ઙ conjuncts in 4/5/6 fonts: there is no 4/5/6 composer, and 4/5/6 expectations are the 7 bytes, which the 4/5/6 fonts draw identically except at 91-94 and B6.

Not bugs (measured):
- Reph struck first on reph-after keyboards gives Shree's own keystroke-order bytes (5E AE 64); AE draws on the preceding glyph, so what is shown matches.
- Candra sign B5 vs B8 and 84 AE vs AF are both spellings the composer accepts.
- The '9C 00' nukta and the lone-vowel-key answers are composer artefacts.
- The 6 words ending in a virama differ only by TextSoft's deliberate visible halant (73 B9 vs the composer's waiting half form D0).

The rest of the read-back differences are lossy fonts (vocalic l signs ૢ ૣ cannot be shown).

Rank BUG-01 and BUG-02 first: they show up in everyday typing on every keyboard. BUG-02's fix changes the last round's truth for રુ/રૂ (66 79 / 66 7C came from feeding ર and the sign as two codes), so ShreeComposerTruthTests data needs updating with it.
